title: Contract credit reconciliation and auto-billing safeguards for enterprise edge cases
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood has seen increased enterprise adoption with committed credits, multi-line contracts, and negotiated overage terms. Recent customer support tickets surfaced 3 classes of failures during mid-cycle adjustments: (1) negative-balance credits when pro-ration rules overlap with manual credit reversals, (2) duplicate credit application after contract amendment + automated credit allocation, and (3) delayed invoice corrections leading to incorrect tax/discount calculations for downstream finance systems.

Problem statement:
We need a deterministic, auditable reconciliation flow and safeguards so that: 1) credits and refunds cannot produce negative balances or double-apply, 2) auto-billing does not charge an overage during a pending credit reversal window, and 3) the security questionnaire and enterprise contract workflows map to clearly defined metering boundaries (what triggers a refund vs. a credit).

Goals:
- Define contract-language-safe reconciliation rules that map to our metering engine and billing ledger.
- Implement auto-billing safeguards that pause or route invoices to review when specific flags/conditions are met (e.g., pending manual credit, contract amendment in last 72h, tax region mismatch).
- Create a small pricing experiment to validate UX and accounting impact when offering automatic mid-cycle credits vs. pro-rated refunds.
- Ensure the flow addresses items commonly raised in security/compliance questionnaires (audit logs, KMS/HSM for adjusting financial metadata, dual-approval for enterprise adjustments).

Scope (what's in/out):
In scope:
- Reconciliation rules for credits, refunds, and proration across hosted and dedicated billing modes.
- Auto-billing hold/fallback policy implementation and UI flags in Console.
- Telemetry/dashboard showing frequency and dollar impact of mid-cycle adjustments.
- Experiment design for 'auto-credit' vs 'manual-refund' for a cohort of customers.

Out of scope:
- Changes to external tax calculation providers (we will pass tax inputs through unchanged).
- Full ERP integration (finance team will handle downstream posting).

Proposed approach:
1) Product & Legal: create canonical mapping doc that translates contract clauses (credit windows, grace periods, overage caps) to platform flags. Attach to contract templates.
2) Billing Engine: add a reconciliation state machine with explicit states: PENDING_ADJUSTMENT, ADJUSTED, HOLD_FOR_REVIEW, FINALIZED. Ensure idempotency keys and audit entries for each transition.
3) Console: add a per-account billing status indicator and one-click 'approve/reject' for holds. Provide recommended roll-forward behaviors for canary customers.
4) Experiment: randomly assign 200 eligible enterprise test accounts to two cohorts for 8 weeks: (A) automatic credit application subject to guardrails; (B) manual support-triggered refunds. Measure time-to-resolution, number of support tickets, and net revenue delta.
5) Security & Compliance: require 2-person approval for adjustments > $5,000; log approvals to the audit stream and include KMS-based metadata stamping for adjustments tied to contract changes.

Telemetry required:
- Count and dollar amount of adjustments by type (credit, refund, reversal, proration) daily.
- Number of invoices held and average hold duration.
- Support ticket volume and median time-to-close for adjustment-related tickets.
- Experiment metrics: cohort revenue, customer satisfaction NPS delta (where available).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement reconciliation state machine + idempotency + audit logging behind a feature flag.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): Console hold UI + API flags; enable for internal accounts.
- Phase 3 (4 weeks): run the experiment on a controlled cohort; monitor telemetry; collect finance and legal sign-off.
- Phase 4: full rollout with enterprise contract templates updated and security questionnaire guidance added to deal desk docs.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect rollback causing double credits. Mitigation: idempotency keys and dry-run mode for 48h before publishing to production; automated invariant checks comparing ledger vs. metering snapshot.
- Risk: experiment reduces short-term revenue. Mitigation: caps on credit amounts during experiment and allow finance to set global offsets.
- Risk: security reviewers require longer lead time. Mitigation: early sync with security to enumerate audit log and KMS expectations; include security reviewers in Phase 1.

Open questions:
- What is the canonical TTL for a "pending adjustment" before auto-finalizing? (Proposed 72h)
- Should tax recalculation trigger a separate review workflow? (Recommend yes for tax-region mismatches)
- How to reflect partial-month credits in customer-facing invoices for transparency? (Design will prototype explanatory line items)

Links & artifacts:
- Mockup: https://drive.redwood.ai/billing/pm/credit-recon-mockup (internal)
- Finance requirements doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Finance+-+Midcycle+Adjustments
- Related Linear thread: PM-27431 (auto-proration ledger)
- Reference PR: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1123 (reconciliation state stubs)
acceptance_criteria: Reconciliation state machine exists with PENDING_ADJUSTMENT/HOLD_FOR_REVIEW/ADJUSTED/FINALIZED states and idempotency keys
Console exposes per-account billing hold and an approve/reject flow for held invoices
Feature flagged experiment runs for defined cohort and telemetry dashboards surface required metrics
Security sign-off documented with audit log schema and KMS metadata requirements
No incidents of duplicate credit application in 72h dry-run validation window
